requirements.title: A type parameter definition has an integer specification, category attribute and declaration list
requirements.source: 7.5.3.1 R732, J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 91, printed 77, lines 3-4.
requirements.definition: A type-param-def-stmt starts with an integer-type-spec, followed by a comma, one type-param-attr-spec, a double colon and a type-param-decl-list. The integer specification may itself have its canonical kind selector. That selector chooses the integer kind of the parameter, whereas the separate KIND or LEN attribute chooses the parameter category. This is not an ordinary component declaration or a PARAMETER attribute statement.
requirements.oracle: The finite corpus has independent compile-only category/selector/list controls and three one-token repairs. Every parameter declaration precedes the component part under R726, and all controls satisfy C746/C747. Negative contracts identify the defining statement's actual separator or integer-prefix condition.
requirements.oracle_limitation: R705/R706/C717 retain INTEGER specification, expression and representation-support ownership. R401 owns list expansion; R733 and R734 own the local descendants. An invalid attempted definition can also strand a header name under C747 or resemble an invalid component statement; those consequences are not substitute R732 causes. Fixture contracts distinguish observed causal messages from prospective parser predicates; observations do not replace independent source and fixture adjudication. Required reporting is not mandatory fatal rejection.
requirements.dependencies: 4.1.2-4.1.3 and 4.2 p2(3), PDF 45-46; R705/R706/C717 and 7.4.3.1 p2/p4, PDF 80; R726/R727, PDF 88, retain canonical ownership of definition order and the header in 7.5.2.1.

requirements.title: A parameter declarator optionally supplies a scalar integer constant default expression
requirements.source: 7.5.3.1 R733, PDF 91, printed 77, line 5; default interpretation in p4, PDF 92.
requirements.definition: A type-param-decl names the parameter and may append an equals sign and a scalar integer constant expression. This expression defines an optional default for either parameter category; it is not a runtime LEN argument expression. Absence of the expression creates no implicit zero or KIND-derived default. A kind selector on INTEGER is a different syntactic item from this default value.

pending.canonical-expression-categories: Pending canonical C401, C1009 and C1014 evidence in this exact default-expression context: distinguish rank-one integer, scalar real and scalar nonconstant integer RHS defects, each with a scalar integer constant repair. Keep those primary owners and any future evidence-link representation separate; existing C701 actual-kind-value cases are not default-expression coverage.

requirements.oracle: Four small admission/repair plans exercise omission, a literal, arithmetic/parenthesized constant defaults and the incomplete equals clause. No value effect is inferred from compilation. Scalar, integer and constant-expression restrictions are retained through their canonical owners rather than new supplementary rejection rules.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A LEN parameter may have runtime actual values in permitted later contexts, but its R733 default still needs a constant expression. A defaulted LEN name does not automatically become a constant-expression primary in the definition. Bare terminal alternatives cannot enforce an implicit literal or statement context. No source-only diagnostic policy is used to turn an unnumbered permission into mandatory rejection.
requirements.dependencies: R732/R734; R403/C401, PDF 45; R1027/C1009, PDF 183; R1032/C1014 and 10.1.12, PDF 187-188. C797 and 7.5.9 p2-p3, PDF 106, govern later arguments and omission; p4 supplies the default's value and conversion.

requirements.title: Every defined parameter name belongs to the same type header
requirements.definition: A parameter name in a type parameter definition statement must occur in the derived-type-stmt of that same derived-type definition. A name in another type header, a host entity or an inherited parameter does not supply a local header entry for a new local declaration. This membership condition is distinct from C747's requirement to define every header name exactly once.
requirements.oracle: Two positive controls and a bounded KIND/LEN membership family use fresh names, complete TYPE/END TYPE pairs and no dependent components. Each negative's only repair is to its own header. A diagnostic must connect the offending parameter definition to that header, at an exact use point or explicitly justified bounded definition relation.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Use names absent from any parent to avoid turning the unlisted-name case into an inherited-name collision. Inherited parameters retain their original definitions and attributes under 7.5.7.2; no new local declaration is manufactured for them. Generic type/name/kind errors, unsupported facilities, crashes, verifier and resource failures cannot establish membership. No compiler observation or self-approval is claimed.
requirements.dependencies: R732/R733; R727 and C736, PDF 88; 7.5.7.2 p1 and its name/inheritance notes, PDF 104-105; 4.2 p2(3), PDF 46. The canonical inheritance and header-definition owners remain outside this catalogue.

requirements.title: Each local header parameter has exactly one definition in that type
requirements.definition: Every type parameter name in a type's derived-type-stmt appears exactly once as a parameter name in a type parameter definition statement of that same definition. Both missing and repeated definitions violate the condition. The constraint does not prescribe definition-statement order or add inherited names to a child's local header list.
requirements.oracle: The finite controls count every local header name once. Missing-definition diagnoses need the particular header name and the matching TYPE definition; repeated-definition diagnoses need the same parameter identity at its repeated declaration. Repairs add one missing definition or remove one repeated name/statement. The header and all unrelated definitions remain unchanged.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Missing definitions cannot be bound to a nonexistent declaration line: a header/END TYPE or related declaration span needs explicit source justification. Do not accept a whole-unit recovery range or generic symbol/constant/function complaint. A duplicate definition can also implicate canonical declaration/name rules; it is one repeated-definition defect, not proof of a distinct internal C747 check. R726 still orders the parameter-definition block before components, and constant-expression dependencies still require their own prior-declaration premises.
requirements.dependencies: R726/R727/C736, PDF 88; R732/R733/C746; 10.1.12 p1(12), PDF 187, for dependent default expressions; 7.5.7.2, PDF 104-105, for inherited definitions. 4.2 p2(3), PDF 46, requires reporting capability, not a specified diagnostic sentence or fatal exit.

requirements.title: The explicit parameter category is KIND or LEN
requirements.source: 7.5.3.1 R734, PDF 92, printed 78, lines 1-2; classification restatement p3, line 6.
requirements.definition: The type-param-attr-spec alternatives are KIND and LEN. They classify a derived-type parameter independently of the kind selector on its INTEGER declaration and independently of its name, default value or eventual use as a component bound or intrinsic kind selector.
requirements.oracle: Two independent compile-only category controls admit both alternatives with valid INTEGER specifications and exact header/definition membership. The general generic-resolution distinction keeps S7.2-003 ownership, including its existing PDT case.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No PARAMETER/POINTER or arbitrary-attribute substitution is advertised as an isolated R734 negative: it can enter component grammar and strand a header name under C747. The closed two-alternative grammar does not itself manufacture another executable restriction or a physical-length assertion. The p3 restatement and informative generic example are accounted without duplicate semantic ownership.
requirements.dependencies: R732; 7.2 p2 and S7.2-003, PDF 76; R737/R738 component declarations, PDF 93; 4.2 p2(3), PDF 46. Existing S7_2_003_valid__pdt remains canonical and is neither copied nor reclassified.

requirements.title: A derived parameter's INTEGER declaration determines its own type and integer kind
requirements.source: 7.5.3.1 p2, PDF 92, printed 78, lines 4-5; R732 integer specification, PDF 91.
requirements.definition: Each derived-type parameter has integer type. Its own integer kind is supplied by the INTEGER specification of the defining statement. With no kind selector, the source explicitly states default integer for a KIND parameter; the same omitted-selector result for a LEN declaration also follows the canonical INTEGER specification/default rule. An explicit INTEGER selector is not overridden by the parameter's KIND/LEN category.

The already existing selected-carrier execution is a finite canonical reuse candidate, not newly authored coverage. Any future all-method witness is independently bounded and must instantiate every method inside its stated boundary.
requirements.oracle_limitation: There are three separate facts: KIND/LEN category, the parameter's INTEGER kind, and its integer value. p2's second sentence specifically names a kind type parameter; the LEN default-kind conclusion is anchored through R732/R705 and 7.4.3.1 p4, not a silent alteration of that wording. Intrinsic KIND parameters' default-integer rule and intrinsic CHARACTER LEN's processor-dependent integer kind are not copied indiscriminately to PDT parameters. Selected integer methods may coincide with default and need not represent an arbitrary default-integer kind identifier. No identifier is narrowed, ordered as a size, or converted into a real payload.

requirements.title: An explicit default expression supplies the value, converted to the parameter's integer kind when necessary
requirements.definition: A parameter declarator containing the optional scalar integer constant expression has a default value determined by that expression. If conversion is necessary, intrinsic assignment supplies a value of the parameter's own integer kind. The statement does not default another declarator, assign a component, or create a default merely because INTEGER's kind selector is absent.

pending.inherited-default-context: Pending a source-reviewed 7.5.7.2 dependency/use connection: a parent parameter with a default and a child with an independent local default should retain the inherited attributes when both actuals are omitted. Check the two small values separately; do not redeclare the inherited parameter in the child or claim full inheritance coverage here.
pending.default-use-context-graph: Pending a finite canonical matrix over declarations, component type specifications, ALLOCATE type specifications, structure-constructor derived-type specifiers, dummy declarations and TYPE IS guards. Classify where omission is permitted under each owner and add one bounded default/explicit-value contrast per applicable role. One declaration program does not cover every default-use context.

requirements.oracle: Planned runtime effects use exact small integer expectations and parameter-inquiry kinds, never floating approximation or storage layouts. Small values are chosen to be independently representable in both source and destination integer methods. Default omission and explicit override are distinguished from parameter declaration syntax and from assigning component values.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The default expression itself must satisfy R733's scalar/integer/constant restrictions even for LEN. The conversion is not a license for out-of-range values, wraparound, a trap oracle, or narrowing an arbitrary kind identifier into a selected method. Mandatory range-18 support is not made optional; only an additional distinct-kind/inventory branch may need a profile. All effects stay run-phase if implementations lack PDT support. No supplementary mandatory diagnostic is invented for this prose interpretation.

requirements.title: Type parameters may be specification-expression primaries inside their derived-type definition
requirements.source: 7.5.3.1 p5, PDF 92, printed 78, lines 10-11, first permission.
requirements.definition: A type parameter may occur as a primary in a specification expression in the definition of that derived type. The permission includes KIND and LEN parameters. It does not admit arbitrary host-variable values into component specifications, move declarations after the component part, or remove the consuming context's stricter component-specification-expression conditions.

pending.specification-use-graph: Pending a finite matrix over parameter INTEGER selectors, parameter defaults, component type-parameter values, lower/upper component bounds and component character-length forms, for local/inherited KIND/LEN primaries. Apply each role's canonical restrictions first; classify inapplicable or constant-only roles rather than treating the broad specification permission as a universal waiver. Existing S7.2 allocation/assignment/dummy effects remain canonical candidates, not automatic coverage.

requirements.oracle: The finite direct plans are run-phase permission witnesses using actual PDT parameter values and independently specified small component lengths/extents. Definition-only admission controls may accompany them but do not replace those effects. The full source-use matrix remains separately pending.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A type parameter is not an object or ordinary variable, as the component note clarifies. Formal LEN use is therefore not interchangeable with a runtime host-variable value. C755/C759 and 10.1.11 p9 still govern component specification expressions; initialized components add C767. Initial plans avoid initialization of LEN-dependent array/character components in the type definition and instead initialize objects after checking their valid extents. No non-required prose rejection or unsupported-feature skip is used.
requirements.dependencies: R726, PDF 88; 7.5.4.1/R737-R740/C754-C755/C759 and its note, PDF 93-94; 7.5.4.6/C767, PDF 96; 10.1.11 p1/p2(15)/p9, PDF 185-187; 9.4.5, PDF 153. Parameter definitions, component rules and later allocation/assignment/dummy mechanisms keep their separate owners.

requirements.title: A KIND parameter may also be a constant-expression primary inside the definition
requirements.source: 7.5.3.1 p5, PDF 92, printed 78, lines 10-11, additional KIND permission.
requirements.definition: A kind type parameter may also serve as a primary in a constant expression in the derived-type definition. The canonical constant-expression rule specifically admits a previously declared KIND parameter of the type being defined. A default value does not turn a bare LEN parameter into such a primary. This is not a blanket ban on every inquiry mentioning LEN; each distinct inquiry route needs its own canonical premises.

requirements.oracle: The three direct plans are runtime effects with small exact integer values and explicit parameter/component type checks. They place every referenced KIND definition before the use and avoid runtime IF as a guard for an invalid constant declaration. Inherited and negative/use-graph connections remain uncredited pending canonical evidence.
requirements.oracle_limitation: R726 orders parameter-definition statements before components, but parameter order for positional arguments is instead 7.5.3.2. The initial plans do not rely on forward references merely because a name is in the TYPE header. Neither a kind selector nor a constant default is exempted from its scalar/integer/constant/support restrictions. Unknown or oversized kind identifiers are never converted to another parameter integer kind; an optional distinct carrier cannot be inferred from SELECTED_INT_KIND returning a successful value.

accounting.rationale: PDF 92 line 3 gives a local header condition and parameterized-type classification, not a new execution requirement.
A nonempty local type-param-name list supplies the stated sufficient condition. R727 owns the header syntax; this is not a new requirement for parameter values or component layout.

The defined type is parameterized when that condition holds. Do not reverse the implication for an extended type: 7.5.7.2 can supply inherited parameters even when its local header adds none. That inheritance is a dependency, not source approval here.
PDF 92 lines 4-5 separates INTEGER type from the omitted-kind-selector statement. Parameter category, own integer kind and default value remain distinct.

PDF 92 line 6 states that the attribute explicitly determines KIND versus LEN category. R734 owns the alternatives and 7.2 owns the general category/generic-resolution distinction. No duplicate local semantic rejection is introduced.
PDF 92 lines 7-9 distinguishes the optional-default condition, expression value, conditional conversion and destination parameter integer kind.
PDF 92 lines 10-11 gives two permissions with different parameter-category conditions and a shared within-definition scope.
Either category may be a specification-expression primary in the definition, subject to the consuming context's canonical rules.
The additional constant-expression permission concerns a KIND parameter; the canonical rule adds the previously declared condition.
A KIND primary can participate in an otherwise valid constant expression. This is not an invented mandatory prose diagnostic.
Both permissions concern the definition of the type whose parameter is referenced, not arbitrary unbound names or general runtime assignment.
The complete PDF 92 note has a matrix example and a KIND-dimension/generic example; its individual premises remain informative.
The first example lists two parameters and defines each with an explicit category. It illustrates R732/C746/C747, not an extra requirement to reproduce this particular type.
The real-method selector parameter has a KIND(0.0) default while its own INTEGER declaration has default kind. The parameter value is not its integer kind or a prescribed byte count.

The LEN parameter's INTEGER specification uses SELECTED_INT_KIND(12), described as potentially nondefault. Selection can coincide with default and does not justify narrowing another arbitrary identifier.

The first parameter supplies a supported real component kind and the LEN parameter supplies both array extents. Component specification-expression rules remain applicable; no physical representation or rounding guarantee follows.
The second example declares its array dimension as KIND, demonstrating that a KIND parameter need not be an intrinsic representation selector and a parameter name does not determine its category.

The stated generic-overload motivation keeps 7.2/S7.2-003 and the canonical generic rules as owners. S7_2_003_valid__pdt is relevant existing finite evidence, not a new execution or a complete generic-use graph.
